verdict.rationale: Wally Cloud runs models on RunAnywhere's hardware rather than the user's, so users can run models too large for a laptop with the same tools. A `--cloud` flag explicitly selects the hosted model, and an OpenAI-compatible endpoint is available. Hosted execution is an explicit choice, never a silent fallback, which fits a user-initiated offload. missing for 10: an explicit statement that cloud use needs no local model download, a documented catalog or size range of the hosted large models, and independent hands-on corroboration of the cloud tier.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can offload very large models to a hosted cloud tier without downloading them when my local hardware is insufficient

citations.quote: Cloud models run on RunAnywhere's hardware instead of the user's, so you can use models too large for a laptop while keeping the same tools.
`--cloud` is an `opencode` flag: it asks for the hosted model rather than one on this machine.
Hosted and local execution are explicit choices. Wally does not silently move a request between them.
